name: Maryland Eats: Restaurants
subtitle: Crab Cakes, Pit Beef & Oysters
description:
Maryland's restaurants, from a jumbo lump crab cake to a snowball on a July night.

Maryland Eats is a free guide to eating in Maryland: 11 crab cake and crab houses, 3 pit beef stands, 8 oyster bars, 4 pupuserías, 4 Ethiopian kitchens, 4 Route 40 Koreatown restaurants and 16 snowball and sweets stops we checked by hand, plus 12,501 restaurants, cafés, bars and bakeries in 366 towns, from Baltimore and Annapolis to Ocean City and Garrett County. No account, no ads.

MARYLAND GUIDES
• Crab Cakes & Crab Houses: jumbo lump and backfin, Lexington Market to Dundalk.
• Baltimore Pit Beef: charcoal-grilled and sliced thin.
• Oyster Bars: raw bars from Baltimore to the Eastern Shore.
• Pupuserías and Ethiopian: Montgomery and Prince George's pupusas, and Silver Spring's Ethiopian kitchens.
• Route 40 Koreatown: Korean restaurants in Ellicott City.
• Snowballs & Sweets: summer snowball stands and more.
• James Beard Honors and Oldest Places.

FIND IT FAST
• Sort by distance, or browse the map by guide.
• Search by name, town, street or dish: "crab cake baltimore", "pit beef", "snowball hampden".
• Filter by town or cuisine, or hide chains.
• Save places, and find hand-checked places from iPhone search (Spotlight).

LIVE DETAILS FROM APPLE MAPS
Tap "Ratings, hours & photos" on any place to open Apple Maps' own place card, with current hours, photos, ratings and directions.

HOW THE LISTS ARE BUILT
Every guide place was checked by hand in fall 2026 against a 2025 or 2026 source: a dated magazine or news story or an official tourism listing. The rest come from Overture Maps open data, kept by a reliability rule tested against the food facilities Montgomery and Anne Arundel counties inspect, plus inspected restaurants the map data missed. Maryland posts no letter grades; Montgomery County places show the county's latest result in its own words with the date, and every other place links the list of local health departments. Website links are checked too. Nothing is ranked by star ratings, and the app computes no grades. Newer restaurant data downloads from the Maryland Eats website when there is some.

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
No account, no tracking, no ads. Your location, if you share it, only sorts lists on your device. Saved places stay on your device.

Places open and close, so check before you go. Spot a mistake? Email nick@eatsranked.com.

An independent app, not affiliated with any restaurant, chain or government agency (including the State of Maryland, the Maryland Department of Health, Montgomery County or Anne Arundel County), or with the James Beard Foundation. James Beard Foundation and James Beard Award are trademarks of the James Beard Foundation. Place data from Overture Maps Foundation (CDLA Permissive 2.0) and others; sources and licenses are on the About tab.

reviewNotes:
1. Purpose and audience: Maryland Eats is a free guide to restaurants in Maryland (the U.S. state). Its focus is the state's own food: 11 crab cake and crab houses, pit beef stands, 8 oyster bars, pupuserías, Ethiopian kitchens, Route 40 Koreatown and 16 snowball and sweets stops, each checked by hand in fall 2026 against a 2025 or 2026 source, plus the James Beard honorees. It also lists 12,501 restaurants, cafés and bars in 366 towns from open map data, checked against Montgomery and Anne Arundel counties' inspected food facilities. It is for residents and visitors deciding where to eat, with no ads, account or tracking.

2. How to use it (no login, no setup, no sample files needed):
- Home → Crab Cakes & Crab Houses (or Baltimore Pit Beef, Oyster Bars, Pupuserías, Ethiopian, Route 40 Koreatown, Snowballs & Sweets, James Beard Honors, Oldest Places, Near Me) → tap any place.
- On a place, tap "Ratings, hours & photos" to open Apple Maps' own place card through MapKit. Directions, Call and Website are below it; further down, Montgomery County places show the county's latest inspection result with its date, and others link the list of Maryland's local health departments in Safari.
- Search from the Home search box by name, town, street or dish ("crab cake baltimore", "pit beef", "snowball hampden").
- The Map tab shows each guide as pins. "My location" and the Nearest sort use location only if allowed, on the device.
- The heart saves a place on the device (Saved tab). The About tab lists the sources, licenses and the independence statement.
- On iPad, a sidebar replaces the tabs; a place opens in the right-hand column.
- Location: if you're outside Maryland (as App Review usually is), the map says so and stays on Maryland, and distance sorting still works from where you are.
- "MD Eats" is the Home Screen name of "Maryland Eats: Restaurants".

3. External services and data:
- Apple MapKit: maps, local search to find a place's Apple Maps listing, and Apple's place card for live hours, photos and ratings.
- Core Location: optional, on-device only, for distance sorting.
- Data updates: at most once a day, the app checks the Maryland Eats website (static files on GitHub Pages) for newer restaurant data and downloads it if there is some. The requests carry no identifiers or location.
- No backend, accounts, analytics, advertising, payments or AI services. The restaurant data is bundled in the app.
- Bundled data sources: Overture Maps Foundation open place data (CDLA Permissive 2.0 and others; license texts are in the app); Montgomery County's food inspections and Anne Arundel County's inspected facilities (public records); James Beard Foundation honors (facts only); and our own research of public websites and local news.
- The website with the privacy policy and support page is static and hosted on GitHub Pages: https://nickstrom5.github.io/maryland-eats/

4. Regional differences: none. The content covers Maryland; the app is offered in the United States and works the same everywhere.

5. Regulated or protected material: the app is not in a regulated industry and includes no protected third-party material. The data is open-licensed or public record, with attribution and licenses on the About tab. Ratings, hours and photos are shown only inside Apple's own place card through MapKit; the app stores no ratings or reviews. Inspection results appear only for Montgomery County, in the county's own words with the date; the app computes no grades and ranks nothing by inspections. Every website link was checked before release, and adult venues are excluded. The app is independent and not affiliated with any restaurant, agency or the James Beard Foundation.
